purpose: Research anchors used to ground the public reasoning-compiler capability map. These are design lessons, not claims that ZTARE has externally matched the papers' results.
coverage_note: This registry covers the v1.1 reasoning-compiler capability map baseline. It is a design-anchor registry, not a complete bibliography for every field ZTARE touches.

anchors.label: Explicit source grounding

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

anchors.design_lesson: Factual work should separate model output from retrieved or local source material, then inspect whether the source is relevant enough to support the answer.
anchors.ztare_implication: Keep source files, evidence refs, compiled evidence, gap records, and report support separate and inspectable.

anchors.label: Attribution and verifiability

sources.title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models
Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines
Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation

anchors.design_lesson: Trustworthy generated text needs sentence- or fact-level support checks; citations and source links are not enough unless the cited source actually supports the claim.
anchors.ztare_implication: Report support, evidence summaries, and claim cards should separate generated wording from source-backed facts, unsupported facts, citation/support gaps, and the repair action that would make the claim admissible.

anchors.label: Source quality

sources.title: SourceBench: Can AI Answers Reference Quality Web Sources?
Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Estimation of Source Reliability
MSRS: Evaluating Multi-Source Retrieval-Augmented Generation

anchors.design_lesson: Source support is not only about whether a source exists. Quality, reliability, freshness, authority, and multi-source synthesis can change whether a cited answer should be trusted.
anchors.ztare_implication: Source readiness, evidence summaries, and report support should keep source type, freshness, authority/reliability hints, backing-file paths, unresolved source-quality gaps, and multi-source synthesis boundaries inspectable.

anchors.label: Intermediate verification

sources.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models

anchors.design_lesson: Reasoning improves when intermediate steps are checked, not only the final answer.
anchors.ztare_implication: Expose run readiness, preflight, support checks, reviews, and saved records as separate project states.

anchors.label: Task-specific interfaces

sources.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering

anchors.design_lesson: Agents and users perform better when the software interface is built around the task's actual actions, files, and feedback.
anchors.ztare_implication: The Workbench should expose project actions, write boundaries, file viewers, and saved history instead of generic chat or generic dashboards.

anchors.label: Durable feedback memory

sources.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

anchors.design_lesson: Feedback improves later attempts when it is preserved and reused across trials.
anchors.ztare_implication: Reviews, next steps, source warnings, run history, action intelligence, and saved records should become durable project state.

anchors.label: Appropriate human reliance

sources.title: Towards Human-AI Deliberation: Design and Evaluation of LLM-Empowered Deliberative AI for AI-Assisted Decision-Making
From Trust to Appropriate Reliance: Measurement Constructs in Human-AI Decision-Making

anchors.design_lesson: The goal of human-AI decision support is not more trust; it is calibrated reliance, explicit disagreement, and enough structure for the human to accept, defer, or reject advice for the right reason.
anchors.ztare_implication: Workbench reviews, next steps, report-support decisions, and saved project files should expose the decision point, backing evidence, unresolved disagreement, and no-change boundary before the human records a decision.

anchors.label: Evaluation discipline

sources.title: AI Agents That Matter

anchors.design_lesson: Accuracy alone is not enough; cost, reproducibility, holdouts, baselines, and overfitting matter.
anchors.ztare_implication: Preserve no-spend checks, frozen evidence, non-claims, missing arms, benchmark artifacts, and public claim boundaries.

anchors.label: Compression progress

sources.title: Interestingness as an Inductive Heuristic for Future Compression Progress

anchors.design_lesson: Future discovery is more plausible after recent compression progress and less plausible after a long flat stretch; exact complexity profiles are only available in bounded formal settings.
anchors.ztare_implication: Use BIC, MDL, proof length, artifact size, and effort as advisory compression proxies; replay them on historical runs before changing loop control.

anchors.label: Model-selection compression

sources.title: Estimating the Dimension of a Model
Modeling by shortest data description

anchors.design_lesson: A better fit is not automatically a better explanation; model complexity and description length need their own pressure.
anchors.ztare_implication: Treat BIC, MDL-style length, proof length, and script length as first-class signals next to raw score movement.

anchors.label: Expression-grammar compression

sources.title: All elementary functions from a single binary operator

anchors.design_lesson: A compact operator basis can express a broad elementary-function vocabulary, which makes grammar reachability a separate question from search quality.
anchors.ztare_implication: Use restricted expression grammars such as `eml_only` as a concrete primitive-composition test: declare the allowed primitives, compose inside them, and reject vocabulary escapes before trusting a fit or score.

anchors.label: Symbolic equation discovery

sources.title: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy)
AI Feynman: A physics-inspired method for symbolic regression
PySR: High-Performance Symbolic Regression in Python and Julia

anchors.design_lesson: Equation discovery works best when search is constrained by structure, simplicity, invariances, and a clear distinction between fit quality and expression complexity.
anchors.ztare_implication: Autoresearch fit loops should show grammar limits, fitted expression, BIC/MDL-style complexity, residual diagnostics, out-of-sample support, and whether a candidate is a simpler explanation or only a better-looking fit.

anchors.label: Forecast calibration

sources.title: ForecastBench: A Dynamic Benchmark of AI Forecasting Capabilities
Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models
Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback

anchors.design_lesson: Forecasting quality depends on dated questions, explicit probabilities, retrieval or aggregation, and later resolution against outcomes.
anchors.ztare_implication: Keep forecast rows, decision-use evidence, resolution timing, calibration scores, and downstream action boundaries separate.

anchors.label: Proxy gaming and leakage

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science
SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents

anchors.design_lesson: Optimizing an imperfect score, leaking target information, or passing visible tests can produce confident but unsupported results.
anchors.ztare_implication: Keep frozen artifacts, hidden checks, ordinary-review gaps, non-claims, and evaluator-gaming catches visible.

anchors.label: Rubric and judge reliability

sources.title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
LLMs are Narcissistic Evaluators

anchors.design_lesson: Rubrics and model judges can be useful, but they carry bias, self-preference, calibration, truthfulness, and benchmark-design risks that must be measured rather than assumed away.
anchors.ztare_implication: Scoring guides, adversarial reviews, evaluator-hardening artifacts, ordinary-review gaps, and non-claims should stay visible next to any score or judge verdict.

anchors.label: Formal proof governance

sources.title: Graph Sequence Learning for Premise Selection
Premise Selection for Theorem Proving by Deep Graph Embedding
DeepSeek-Prover-V2: Advancing Formal Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Subgoal Decomposition

anchors.design_lesson: Formal proof systems need premise selection, subgoal decomposition, kernel checking, and proof-state feedback rather than free-form proof text alone.
anchors.ztare_implication: Treat LeanMill outputs as governed formal artifacts: parse the statement, compile through Lean, audit axioms, preserve proof attempts, and separate formalization failures from proof failures.

anchors.label: Stateful tool use

sources.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
tau2-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment

anchors.design_lesson: Tool agents must follow domain rules, coordinate with user state, and leave verifiable state changes.
anchors.ztare_implication: Workbench actions should show the rule, target files, confirmation boundary, saved-record path, and resulting project state.

anchors.label: Computer-use execution

sources.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
CRAB: Cross-environment Agent Benchmark for Multimodal Language Model Agents
TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
WindowsWorld: A Process-Centric Benchmark of Autonomous GUI Agents in Professional Cross-Application Environments

anchors.design_lesson: Real computer-use and web-agent work is brittle unless execution, subgoals, file or app state, and evaluation results are inspected.
anchors.ztare_implication: Treat the Workbench UI as an execution surface over repo state; success requires changed files, checks, saved records, and refreshed read models.

anchors.label: Structural code memory

sources.title: Codebase-Memory: Tree-Sitter-Based Knowledge Graphs for LLM Code Exploration via MCP
DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp

anchors.design_lesson: Large codebases need persistent structural memory over symbols, call paths, architecture decisions, and change impact; repeated file-by-file exploration wastes context and misses dependencies.
anchors.ztare_implication: Federate the existing architecture index, graph, primitive recall, route contracts, and map validators into repository-memory questions instead of adding another disconnected map.
